speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is happening, can you tell me if your vomiting is projectile and if you have noticed any weight loss or failure to thrive?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The crying that worsens when the belly is touched is a significant finding. Can you tell me if you have noticed any "currant jelly" colored stools or blood mixed with the stool? Also, is the abdomen firm and tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever, vomiting, or diarrhea is noted, and the birth history is uncomplicated. Does your baby pass stools normally, or do you observe an "olive-like" mass in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Palpation; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

text: The abdominal palpation shows tenderness specifically in the left lower quadrant, which is an unusual finding for the conditions we have discussed so far. Have you noticed any redness or swelling in the scrotum or groin area, which could indicate a hernia? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Palpation, Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby's stool passage is abnormal and the distension is worsening; can you tell me if there is visible gas (bloating) in the abdomen? Also, have you noticed any vomiting, specifically if it is green or bilious? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
